To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synchronizing movements to the sounds of a partner enhances likeability of the partner.
synchronizing movements with a partner can influence ratings of that partner's likeability.
synchronising movements to sounds attributed to another person can influence likeability of a virtual partner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social nature of music, and how music can influence social behaviour.
the role of sound in social interaction and how this can influence the perception of a partner.
the social consequences of synchronising movements with sounds, which may be relevant to the study of music, dance and social interaction more broadly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
synchronisation with a virtual partner can enhance ratings of likeability, but only when the partner is believed to be a human being.
synchronisation with sounds attributed to another person enhances ratings of likeability, and that this is mediated by the attribution of sounds to another person.
the synchronisation of movements with sounds of a virtual human partner can influence ratings of partner likeability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synchronising with sounds of another person can enhance likeability of that person, but only if the sounds are attributed to that person.
synchronising movements to a virtual partner enhances likeability.
synchronisation can enhance social bonding in virtual interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synchrony of movements with sounds attributed to a partner can enhance partner likeability, and that this effect is not limited to synchrony with a visible partner, but is possible with interaction involving sound alone.
people are more likely to like a person if they move in time to sounds that they believe that person has made.
the synchronisation of actions with sound can enhance likeability of a person, even in the absence of any visual cues.
